page: Microsoft Azure L32as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz. Provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, the instance delivers 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The platform supplies 256 GB of system memory, providing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a direct-attached local storage allocation of 7,679 GB NVMe SSD. Discrete GPU accelerators are not present on this instance type.

Performance metrics reflect strong single-threaded CPU capabilities, with top-quartile results in stress-ng single-core tests and Geekbench 6 evaluations. Instruction set extensions, including AVX-512, VAES, and SHA-NI, drive top-tier cryptographic throughput as demonstrated by strong PassMark encryption scores. Multi-threaded compute benchmarks, including multi-core stress-ng, PassMark database operations, and memory bandwidth, maintain steady mid-tier performance. Uncached memory throughput measures 74.7 GB/s for read operations and 55.71 GB/s for writes under large block transfers.

The integration of 7.68 TB of local NVMe SSD storage delivers high I/O throughput natively without relying on external network-attached volumes, offering favorable resource density for high-throughput operational requirements. Tradeoffs include ephemeral persistence considerations inherent to local NVMe media and the absence of complimentary public IPv4 addressing. The configuration is aligned with transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, Elasticsearch clusters, and high-capacity analytical caching layers.
description: Microsoft Azure L32as_v4 is a storage-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at 3.7 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance features 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores, 256 GB of RAM, and 7,679 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage without discrete GPUs. In synthetic benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong single-core execution and cryptographic throughput, scoring in the top quartile in Geekbench and PassMark encryption tests, while overall multi-core and memory bandwidth remain in the middle tier. By bundling expansive low-latency NVMe disk space with an 8 GB per vCPU memory footprint, it eliminates external storage overhead for I/O-intensive systems. The instance exhibits a well-balanced profile for transactional databases, distributed storage nodes, NoSQL databases, large-scale indexing engines, and analytical data processing.
